subproblem.title: Coordinates of the lattice face map b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : Fin k → Fin P be injective, let b : Fin P → ℤ and let y ∈ Euclid k. Put e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Euclid P and Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j • e_{ι(j)} ∈ Euclid P, where toLp(b) is the vector with coordinates (b_i : ℝ). Then (i) Φ(y)_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m for every m : Fin k, and (ii) Φ(y)_l = b_l for every l : Fin P with ι(m) ≠ l for all m : Fin k.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (ι : Fin k → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ) (y : Euclid k), Function.Injective ι → (∀ m, (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (ι m) = (b (ι m) : ℝ) + y m) ∧ (∀ l, (∀ m, ι m ≠ l) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) l = (b l : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) ∈ Euclid P. toLp(b) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P. Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j • e_{ι(j)}. For v ∈ Euclid P, v_l (written v l in Lean, i.e. ofLp v l) is the l-th coordinate.

1. Coordinates in Euclid P are additive and ℝ-linear: (u + v)_l = u_l + v_l and (c • v)_l = c · v_l. Also (Σ_j v_j)_l = Σ_j (v_j)_l (WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply). Moreover toLp(b)_l = (b_l : ℝ). Since e_i = toLp(Pi.single i 1), (e_i)_l = 1 if l = i and (e_i)_l = 0 otherwise (Pi.single_apply).
2. Hence for every l : Fin P, Φ(y)_l = b_l + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j · (e_{ι(j)})_l = b_l + Σ_{j : Fin k} (if ι(j) = l then y_j else 0).
3. Proof of (i). Fix m : Fin k and take l = ι(m) in step 2. For j ≠ m, injectivity of ι gives ι(j) ≠ ι(m), so the j-th summand is 0. The m-th summand is y_m. Hence the sum equals y_m (Finset.sum_eq_single), and Φ(y)_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m.
4. Proof of (ii). Fix l : Fin P with ι(m) ≠ l for all m : Fin k. Then every summand in step 2 is 0, so the sum is 0 and Φ(y)_l = b_l. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinates are additive and linear. toLp(b)_l = b_l, and (e_i)_l = 1 if l = i, else 0.
Hence Φ(y)_l = b_l + Σ_j (if ι(j) = l then y_j else 0).
At l = ι(m), injectivity of ι makes every summand except j = m vanish (Finset.sum_eq_single), giving b_{ι(m)} + y_m.
For l outside the range of ι every summand vanishes, giving b_l.

audit.reason: The proposition includes precisely the stated injectivity hypothesis and both coordinate conclusions. Linearity, the single-vector coordinate formula, and finite-sum evaluation prove both clauses. Injectivity isolates the unique contributing summand. This is a genuine shared obligation with no dependency on the parent.
